title: I shipped Echoes of the Deep 1.0 using AI as a development copilot — here’s what actually helped
author: EyeApprehensive3982
selftext:
I finally shipped **Echoes of the Deep 1.0**, a Godot 4 pixel-art underwater game, and AI was part of my development workflow throughout the project.

I didn’t use it as a one-click “make a game” solution. Most of the useful work came from repeatedly iterating on very specific systems: GDScript architecture, debugging, localization, UI revisions, balancing ideas, procedural audio/visual experimentation and finding regressions after large changes.

One of the biggest problems I ran into was architecture. The main script became far too large, so during the final development phase I separated systems into managers/services for bosses, worlds, progression, localization, saves, premium content and active-dive gameplay.

I also learned that AI-generated code still needs aggressive verification. Some of the worst bugs came from duplicate localization keys, UI containers fighting their minimum sizes and changes that worked statically but needed real runtime testing.

The final game mixes incremental progression with manual submarine navigation, sonar timing, resource collection, hazards and bullet-hell boss fights across 20 depths.

AI was used for programming assistance, debugging, localization, UI iteration and selected visual/audio asset work. Everything was reviewed, changed and integrated as part of the project.

If anyone here is building a larger Godot project with AI assistance, my biggest takeaway is: **split systems early. A giant main script becomes extremely expensive to iterate on, with or without AI.**

The released game is here if anyone wants to see the result:  
[**https://caseros.itch.io/echoes-of-the-deep**](https://caseros.itch.io/echoes-of-the-deep)
